newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair says budget leak charges "absurd".
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair says budget leak charges "absurd".

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair dismissed opposition Conservative party charges that parts of Wednesday's budget had been leaked as "absurd".

"As far as I am aware all that Treasury officials have done is confirm that what we said that we would do before the election we would indeed do," Blair said in response to questioning from Conservative leader William Hague.
The Conservatives have complained that Treasury officials confirmed a media report that the government would end tax relief on private medical care for elderly people.
The Conservatives' main finance spokesman, Peter Lilley, has demanded that Ann Taylor, leader of the House of Commons, make an emergency statement at 1430 GMT about the case.
Taylor has agreed to make a statement, delaying the budget speech by Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown.

But Labour sources say the party made clear in the run-up to the May 1 election which swept it to power that it would use the savings from scrapping tax relief on private medical insurance for over-60s to pay for a cut in value added tax on home heating bills to five percent from eight percent.

The pledge was one of four -- to cut VAT on fuel, to end the medical insurance tax relief, to impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities and to leave income tax rates unchanged -- made repeatedly before the election, they said.
